openings.claim: Explore a removable geometric cage: two strip guides capture accessible nonworking plate margins, a third strip stops longitudinal travel, and a fourth forms a removable gate. Attach the strip assembly through the existing carriage slots. This is a fabrication candidate, not demonstrated retention.
openings.delta: Change the retaining dependency from magnetic attraction or contact friction to boundary contact carried by the slotted carriage and steel strips. Drill strips only; bend them with pliers only if their section permits. Keep the marked working edge and stroke clearance unobstructed, leave the carriage on its rails, and make no plate or carriage alterations.
openings.prediction: If capture gaps and elastic deflection together remain below 1 mm, both plates should remain within the displacement limit despite their differing magnet pull checks. The nearest rival is a bolted strip bridge pressing cork pads against the plate: that rival depends on preload and friction. Movement with low preload but intact capture boundaries would defeat the cage prediction; retention only after tightening would favor friction.
openings.probe: First inspect slot access, strip bendability, available margins and clearance with the ruler. Proceed only if a complete capture geometry is achievable. Compare cage and cork bridge as the two configurations, with at most three twenty-stroke runs and three timed removal/return checks each. Reserve the final run for the spare and its removal for thick gloves. Mark and measure position before and after strokes; use screwdriver release at the gate without touching the working edge. Reject a candidate above 1 mm or sixty seconds. Stop if fabrication exceeds eighty minutes or observations exceed twenty minutes; insufficient completed comparisons remain inconclusive.
assumptions: Existing slots accept the supplied bolts and permit strip attachment without obstructing rails or stroke clearance.
Unmarked margins permit capture in every escape direction; strip stiffness, achievable gaps and glove access are unknown.
Three checks cannot establish dependable service performance.

assessment: The weak spare makes magnetic interchangeability doubtful. Mechanical capture offers a discriminating candidate, but unknown attachment geometry and strip capacity prevent a feasibility claim.
